s2.p1: There is **no WDSF member federation** in Papua New Guinea. In Oceania, only Australia and New Zealand belong. Here, dance thrives in singsing, and hip hop.
s2.p2: In 2015, PNG student **Peter Karua** danced Standard at his university in the Philippines. His hope: to ==teach his people== the basics.

s3.p: dance at the **Goroka Show** in the Highlands, held each September near Independence Day. Started by Australian patrol officers, it reached its ==70th edition== in 2026.

s4.p1: At the 1957 Goroka Show, over **200** Asaro men appeared in clay masks, bodies painted white. They won ==first prize==.
s4.p2: Legend says mud-covered warriors were taken for **ghosts**. In 1969, a Mudman photo appeared in National Geographic.

s5.name: SING-SING
s5.p: A gathering of **dance, drums and song**: feathers, face paint and kundu drums. The Mount Hagen Show began in 1961 to unite Highland tribes.

s5.name: DUKDUK
s5.p: Only men dance these cone-masked spirits of a **secret society**. Today they arrive **by canoe** at dawn to open the National Mask Festival in Kokopo.

s6.p: Baining men dance at night in **bark-cloth masks** until daybreak, some leaping through a bonfire. Masks are made for ==one ceremony== only, then thrown away or destroyed.

s7.p: Crew **Wan Squad** wins Adult gold at the World Hip Hop Dance Championship in Phoenix, USA. Dancers from ==55 countries== competed.
s7.p2: Wan Squad **defends its title** in Arizona: back-to-back gold for Papua New Guinea.
